topic: Kill Bookmark Lookups Before They Deadlock You
postText:
Two concurrent transactions updating entirely different business records can still crash each other with error 1205 deadlock. In high-throughput healthcare IT systems, this happens when doctors concurrently prescribe medication while stock inventory reconciliation runs in the background.

Root cause: bookmark lookups. When an UPDATE targets a non-clustered secondary index without covering all referenced columns, the database acquires an Exclusive (X) lock on secondary index nodes, then jumps to clustered index to fetch remainder data. If Transaction A updates Index X then requests Clustered Y, while Transaction B updates Clustered Y and requests Index X, the database detects a cyclic dependency and kills one session.

Fixing this requires zero infrastructure spend. First, enforce deterministic lock order: sort all IDs in application memory ascending before executing batch mutations. Second, convert secondary indexes to covering indexes using INCLUDE clauses. Engine never touches the clustered table; the lookup race condition disappears.

Have you ever resolved a nasty production deadlock simply by reordering payload arrays or adding a covering index instead of bumping database hardware?
